You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Versum Materials, Inc. (realized 3–5-year record)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY the realized
> post-transaction record within the fixed outcome window. It contains no closing-time
> structural information.

## Outcome window
- The outcome window is the fixed 3–5-year realized record following the 2016 separation, i.e. approximately 2019–2021. The registrant's last independent annual report was its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2018, filed November 21, 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001660690-18-000165, Form 10-K]

## Realized trajectory within the window
- On January 28, 2019, Versum Materials, Inc. ("Versum") and Entegris, Inc. ("Entegris") issued a joint press release announcing their entry into an agreement and plan of merger between Versum and Entegris. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-017837, Form 8-K]
- On April 12, 2019, prior to entering a new merger agreement, Versum delivered to Entegris a written notice terminating the previously announced Entegris merger agreement (dated January 27, 2019); Versum paid Entegris a termination fee of $140 million, and Versum's special meeting of stockholders scheduled for April 26, 2019 was cancelled. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-104578, Form 8-K]
- Also on April 12, 2019, Versum entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany ("Parent"), and EMD Performance Materials Holding, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent, under which each outstanding Versum share (subject to customary exceptions) would be converted into the right to receive $53.00 per share in cash, without interest. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-104578, Form 8-K]
- The Merck merger agreement provided a termination fee of $235 million payable by Versum under specified circumstances (including a change of board recommendation or termination to accept a Superior Proposal) and an outside date of April 13, 2020, extendable to July 13, 2020 in certain circumstances to obtain regulatory clearances. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-104578, Form 8-K]

## Realized terminal outcome (best-documented scalar)
- On October 7, 2019, pursuant to the April 12, 2019 Merger Agreement, Merger Sub merged with and into Versum, with Versum surviving as the surviving corporation and a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Merck KGaA. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]
- At the effective time on October 7, 2019, each outstanding share of Versum common stock (subject to customary exceptions and appraisal rights) was automatically converted into the right to receive $53.00 per share in cash, without interest; the merger consideration was funded with cash on hand and Merck term-loan facilities. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]
- In connection with the completion, all outstanding obligations under Versum's Credit Agreement dated September 30, 2016 were repaid and its commitments terminated, and Versum's 5.500% Senior Notes due 2024 were satisfied and discharged (redemption noticed for October 16, 2019). [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]

## Documented disruption at the organization/management interface
- At the effective time, all directors then in office — Guillermo Novo, Jacques Croisetière, Seifi Ghasemi, Dr. Yi Hyon Paik, Thomas J. Riordan, Susan C. Schnabel, and Ambassador Alejandro D. Wolff — resigned from the board and its committees, and were replaced by five individuals designated in connection with the transaction. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]
- Immediately following the effective time, certain officers — Guillermo Novo, George G. Bitto, Michael Valente, and Edward C. Shober — ceased to serve in their roles; Versum appointed John J. (Jeff) White, who had served as Senior Vice President of the Delivery Systems & Services segment since 2016, as President, and Monica Elliott, an executive of the acquirer, as Chief Financial Officer. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]
- The bylaws of Versum were amended and restated in their entirety at the effective time to become the bylaws of the former Merger Sub. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]

## Delisting and deregistration
- On October 7, 2019, Versum notified the New York Stock Exchange of the completion of the merger and requested suspension of trading and the filing of a Form 25 to delist and deregister the common stock under Section 12(b); the NYSE halted trading prior to market open on October 7, 2019, and Versum stated it intended to file a Form 15 to suspend its reporting obligations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K]
- Versum filed a Form 15-12B on October 18, 2019 to deregister and suspend its Securities Exchange Act reporting obligations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-269927, Form 15-12B]

## Outcome summary and no-record note (§4)
- The realized outcome within the fixed window is that the registrant, after briefly agreeing to and then terminating a stock-for-stock combination with Entegris (terminated April 12, 2019, $140 million fee), was acquired for cash at $53.00 per share by Merck KGaA on October 7, 2019, whereupon its incumbent board and named executive officers departed, its NYSE listing was terminated, and it deregistered from SEC reporting (Form 15-12B filed October 18, 2019). [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-263471, Form 8-K; SEC accession 0001193125-19-104578, Form 8-K; SEC accession 0001193125-19-269927, Form 15-12B]
- After deregistration in October 2019 the business became a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Merck KGaA, and no separate public 3–5-year operating record (segment financials, impairment, divestiture, or comparable scalar) for the acquired business is available in the registrant's own subsequent filings. Consistent with the no-record rule, any post-acquisition operating trajectory is coded uncertain / bounded rather than inferred from the acquirer's consolidated results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-269927, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
